messages.content: is i hear music the same as i listen to music?
not always. you can hear music from another room without trying to. listening usually is something you choose to do, giving time to the sound.
make that explanation shorter.
you can hear without trying. listening usually is something you choose to do.
can i hear someone but not understand their words?
yes. hearing a voice does not always mean you understand what was said. the sound may be quiet, far away, or in a language you do not know.
now write a request asking my brother to listen to my story.
please listen to my story.
what if i ask did you hear the story?
that asks whether he heard it, often before now. it is different from asking him to listen while you tell it.
make a question asking whether he understood the story.
did you understand the story?
can he answer yes to hearing and no to understanding?
yes. he could say: i heard you, but i did not understand that part. could you explain it again?
only give that reply.
i heard you, but i did not understand that part. could you explain it again?
write a story about a family bringing a meal outside and then changing where they eat. do not make the whole day wrong.

a family carried bread, fruit, and water into the garden for lunch. the child put a page with a drawing on the table. he wanted to show it while they ate. before everyone sat down, the wind began moving the paper and making the table hard to use. the mother took the drawing inside so the wind could not carry it away. the father asked whether they should eat in the kitchen and come back to the garden later. they brought the food in and sat at the kitchen table. the child put the drawing next to the bread, where everyone could see it. after lunch, they went outside for a short walk. the meal had moved, but the day still had room for the things they wanted.
what made them change the meal place?
the wind was moving the paper and making the outside table hard to use.
did they lose all the food?
no. the story says they brought the food inside. it does not say food was lost.
why did the child still want the drawing in the kitchen?
he wanted to show it during the meal. he still wanted that even though the meal was now inside.
use a different word in the last part.
the child still wanted to show the drawing, even after they moved inside.
what stayed the same about their plan?
they ate together and looked at the drawing. they also spent time outside later.
finish with a quiet moment after the walk.
when they returned, the child put the drawing on the shelf. the family sat for a while with the window open, listening to the wind from inside.
i can hear my neighbor playing music, and i am trying to read. i want to ask if they can turn it down without saying they always do this.
you could say: hello. i am trying to read and can hear the music. could you turn it down a little, please?
should i say they are trying to stop me reading?
not unless you know that is their reason. hearing the music does not tell you why they are playing it.
can i just say what i need now?
yes. saying what is happening now and making a clear request is enough. you do not need to say it always happens.
make it a little shorter.
could you turn the music down a little, please? i am trying to read.
what if they say they did not know i could hear it?
you can use that information without saying they knew all along. you could say: thanks for understanding. i can hear it through the wall.
only give that reply without the explanation.
thanks for understanding. i can hear it through the wall.
now they turn it down. give me a short thank you.
thank you. that helps.
only give the request again.
could you turn the music down a little, please? i am trying to read.
i have three groups of objects. each group has two objects. how many objects do i have?
you have six objects.
if i take one object out, can i make just two full groups of two with the objects left?
yes. two groups of two use four objects, and one other object is left without a group.
how many objects are left in all after i take that one out?
five objects are in the group.
can all five be put into full groups of two without anything left?
no. two groups use four objects, leaving one without a group.
explain that with the group size first.
each group needs two objects. five objects can make two full groups, with one object left.
now i add a new object to the group.
then there are six objects again, enough to make three full groups of two.
is the new object the same as the one i took out?
not from your words. you said a new object. it can bring the number back to six without being the same object as before.
only give the number of full groups i can make now.
three full groups.
my sister likes music i do not usually choose. today i listened with her and liked one song.
you found one song you liked while listening with her. that does not have to change everything else you enjoy.
i do not want her to think i like all her music now.
you can be specific. you could say: i liked that song we heard today. would you tell me its name?
what if i only liked the first part?
then say that. i liked the first part of that song is different from saying you liked the whole thing.
write a kind message with that detail.
i liked the first part of the song we heard today. could you tell me its name?
why not say the rest was wrong?
because what you like is not always a fact about what is right for everyone. you can say what worked for you without making a rule for her taste.
use a shorter explanation.
you can like one part without saying the other parts are wrong for everyone.
now she asks if i want to hear more. i am tired and want quiet.
you could say: i would like to hear more another time, but i need quiet now.
i have not chosen another time. leave that out.
thank you for asking, but i need quiet now.
can i say i have been to the library?
yes. it can tell someone you have visited the library before. context helps make the meaning clear.
give an example of when that sentence is useful.
if someone asks whether you know the library from a visit, you can say yes, i have been to the library.
can i say i went to the library yesterday too?
yes. that gives a specific time for the visit: yesterday.
if someone asks where i was yesterday, which is more useful?
i went to the library yesterday is more useful because it answers the question about that day.
what if they ask whether i know the new library from a visit?
you could say: yes, i have been to the new library.
does that say i was there today?
no. it does not give today as the time. you would need to add when you went if that is important.
now tell them i went this morning.
i went to the new library this morning.
only give the sentence with have been again.
i have been to the new library.
write a story about a person taking a phone message for her father. she should give what was said without adding her own ideas as facts.

a daughter answered the phone while her father was in the garden. the person calling said that the library had his book and asked him to call before evening. the daughter wrote those details on a page. she thought it might mean a book he wanted to read was ready, but she did not write that as part of the message. when her father came inside, she gave him the page and said who had called. he knew what the message was about and made the call. she had not needed to know the whole reason to pass on the words he needed.
what did she write down?
the library had his book and wanted him to call before evening.
why did she not write her own idea as a fact?
she did not know that her idea was right. adding it could change what her father thought the person on the phone had said.
what could she say if she wanted to tell him her idea too?
she could say: this is the message they gave. i thought it might be about the book you wanted, but they did not say that.
make that answer shorter.
this is their message. i have an idea about it, but they did not give that as a reason.
did the message stop being useful because she did not know the reason?
no. it still gave her father the information he needed to call back.
finish with the page kept until the call is done.
he put the page near the phone while calling. after the conversation, he said thank you for keeping the message clear.
my story says a child found a key near the door and gave it to her mother. change mother to father and keep everything else.
a child found a key near the door and gave it to her father.
why did you not change her to his?
because the child can still be a girl giving the key to her father. changing the parent does not change the child.
now make the child a boy too.
a child found a key near the door and gave it to his father.
can child still work for a boy?
yes. child is a general word that can be used for a boy or a girl.
now make it two children, without saying who is a boy or a girl.
two children found a key near the door and gave it to their father.
does their tell us there are two keys?
no. their goes with the children here. the story still says a key, so it gives one key.
only change door to window now.
two children found a key near the window and gave it to their father.
what stayed the same in that last change?
the two children, the one key, and giving it to their father stayed the same. only the place changed.
